records.source: בְּ֭נִי שְׁמֹ֣ר אֲמָרָ֑י וּ֝מִצְוֺתַ֗י תִּצְפֹּ֥ן אִתָּֽךְ׃
records.gloss: My son, keep my sayings, and my commandments treasure up with you.
pieces: My son, hold on to what I say, \q and keep my commands safe like treasure.

L.1: My son, keep my sayings, \q and treasure up my commandments with you.

R.1: My son, remember what I say. \q Value my commands like treasure.

decisions.choice: keep ... treasure up: as in 2:1
decisions.reason: The chapter opens as chapter 2 did, with the verb for hiding treasure (tsaphan).

records.heading: The young man and the adulteress

records.source: שְׁמֹ֣ר מִצְוֺתַ֣י וֶחְיֵ֑ה וְ֝תוֹרָתִ֗י כְּאִישׁ֥וֹן עֵינֶֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: Keep my commandments and live, and my teaching like [the] pupil of your eyes.
pieces: Keep my commands and you will live; \q guard my teaching as carefully as the pupil of your eye.

L.2: Keep my commandments and live, \q and my teaching like [the] pupil of your eyes.

R.2: Obey my commands, and you will live. \q Protect my teaching the way you protect your eyes.

decisions.choice: the pupil of your eyes: what you protect most carefully
decisions.reason: The word (ishon) means "little man", the tiny reflection seen in another's eye. The eye's pupil is guarded by instinct (Deuteronomy 32:10; Psalm 17:8). The same word is used for the middle of the night in verse 9.

decisions.choice: keep and live: as in 4:4
decisions.reason: The command is also a promise.

records.source: קָשְׁרֵ֥ם עַל־אֶצְבְּעֹתֶ֑יךָ כָּ֝תְבֵ֗ם עַל־ל֥וּחַ לִבֶּֽךָ׃
records.gloss: Bind them on your fingers; write them on [the] tablet of your heart.
pieces: Tie them around your fingers; \q inscribe them on your heart as on a tablet.

L.3: Bind them on your fingers; \q write them on [the] tablet of your heart.

R.3: Keep them close, like a ring on your finger. \q Remember them as if they were written on your heart.

decisions.choice: bind ... write: as in 3:3 and Deuteronomy 6:8
decisions.reason: The fingers may suggest a ring or a reminder tied to the hand, always in sight.

records.source: אֱמֹ֣ר לַֽ֭חָכְמָה אֲחֹ֣תִי אָ֑תְּ וּ֝מֹדָ֗ע לַבִּינָ֥ה תִקְרָֽא׃
records.gloss: Say to wisdom, My sister [are] you, and kinsman to understanding you will call,
pieces: Tell wisdom, "You are my sister," \q and give understanding the name of dearest friend,

L.4: Say to wisdom, "You [are] my sister," \q and call understanding [your] close relative,

R.4: Love wisdom like a member of your family. \q Make understanding your closest friend.

decisions.choice: my sister: a word of love for a bride
decisions.reason: In the Song of Songs the bridegroom calls his bride "my sister" (Song of Songs 4:9–10). The son is to love Wisdom as his own, so that the strange woman has no place.

decisions.choice: close relative: kin, intimate friend
decisions.reason: The word (moda) means a kinsman (Ruth 2:1, in a related form), someone one belongs to.

records.source: לִ֭שְׁמָרְךָ מֵאִשָּׁ֣ה זָרָ֑ה מִ֝נָּכְרִיָּ֗ה אֲמָרֶ֥יהָ הֶחֱלִֽיקָה׃
records.gloss: to keep you from a strange woman, from a foreign [woman] [who] makes smooth her sayings.
pieces: so that they keep you from the woman who is not yours, \q the outsider with her flattering words.

L.5: to keep you from [the] strange woman, \q from [the] foreign [woman who] makes her sayings smooth.

R.5: They will keep you away from a woman who belongs to another man \q and from her sweet talk.

decisions.choice: the strange and foreign woman: the words of 2:16
decisions.reason: The verse repeats 2:16 almost exactly and introduces the story that follows.

records.source: כִּ֭י בְּחַלּ֣וֹן בֵּיתִ֑י בְּעַ֖ד אֶשְׁנַבִּ֣י נִשְׁקָֽפְתִּי׃
records.gloss: For at [the] window of my house, through my lattice I looked down,
pieces: Once, from the window of my house, \q I looked down through the lattice,

L.6: For at [the] window of my house, \q through my lattice I looked down,

R.6: Once I was looking out through the window of my house.

decisions.choice: I looked down, as the Hebrew text has it
alternatives: she looks out (the ancient Greek translation)
decisions.reason: In the Hebrew the father watches from his window. The ancient Greek translation has the woman looking out of her window for a young man.

decisions.choice: lattice: a wooden screen over a window
decisions.reason: Windows had latticework instead of glass (Judges 5:28). One could see out without being seen.

records.source: וָאֵ֤רֶא בַפְּתָאיִ֗ם אָ֘בִ֤ינָה בַבָּנִ֗ים נַ֣עַר חֲסַר־לֵֽב׃
records.gloss: and I saw among the simple; I noticed among the sons a youth lacking heart,
pieces: and among the naive I saw, \q among the young men I noticed, \q a youth with no sense,

L.7: and I saw among the simple, \q I noticed among the sons, \q a young man lacking heart,

R.7: I saw a group of young men who did not know much about life. \q One of them had no sense at all.

decisions.choice: the simple: the naive of 1:4
decisions.reason: The young man is one of the simple (petayim), the people chapter 1 was written for (1:4, 22).

decisions.choice: lacking heart: without sense
decisions.reason: As in 6:32.

records.source: עֹבֵ֣ר בַּ֭שּׁוּק אֵ֣צֶל פִּנָּ֑הּ וְדֶ֖רֶךְ בֵּיתָ֣הּ יִצְעָֽד׃
records.gloss: passing in the street beside her corner, and [the] way of her house he strode,
pieces: walking down the street near her corner, \q stepping out along the road to her house,

L.8: passing along the street beside her corner, \q and he strode [on the] way to her house,

R.8: He was walking down the street near the corner where she lived, \q toward her house.

decisions.choice: passing ... strode: drifting toward trouble
decisions.reason: He is not said to be looking for her, but he walks the road that leads to her house (5:8).

records.source: בְּנֶֽשֶׁף־בְּעֶ֥רֶב י֑וֹם בְּאִישׁ֥וֹן לַ֝֗יְלָה וַאֲפֵלָֽה׃
records.gloss: in [the] twilight, in [the] evening of [the] day, in [the] pupil of [the] night and darkness.
pieces: at dusk, as the day turned to evening, \q as the black of night came on.

L.9: in [the] twilight, in [the] evening of [the] day, \q in [the] middle of [the] night and darkness.

R.9: It was getting dark. \q Evening was turning into night.

decisions.choice: twilight ... night and darkness: time passing
decisions.reason: The line moves from dusk to full darkness, as if the father watched for a long time. The word for "middle" is the "pupil" of verse 2: the black center of the night.

records.source: וְהִנֵּ֣ה אִ֭שָּׁה לִקְרָאת֑וֹ שִׁ֥ית ז֝וֹנָ֗ה וּנְצֻ֥רַת לֵֽב׃
records.gloss: And look, a woman to meet him, [in the] garment of a prostitute and guarded of heart.
pieces: Then out came a woman to meet him, \q dressed as a prostitute, her mind full of schemes.

L.10: And look, a woman [came] to meet him, \q [in the] garment of a prostitute and guarded of heart.

R.10: Just then a woman stepped out toward him. \q She was dressed like a prostitute, and she was planning to trick him.

decisions.choice: guarded of heart: keeping her real purpose hidden
alternatives: with a heart set on her goal
decisions.reason: Her heart is "guarded" (natsur): she shows nothing of what she intends. The son was told to guard his heart (4:23); she guards hers to deceive.

decisions.choice: the garment of a prostitute: dressed like one
decisions.reason: She is a married woman (verse 19), but she dresses like a prostitute (Genesis 38:14–15).

records.source: הֹמִיָּ֣ה הִ֣יא וְסֹרָ֑רֶת בְּ֝בֵיתָ֗הּ לֹא־יִשְׁכְּנ֥וּ רַגְלֶֽיהָ׃
records.gloss: Boisterous [is] she and rebellious; in her house her feet do not stay.
pieces: She is loud and unruly; \q her feet never stay at home.

L.11: She [is] loud and defiant; \q in her house her feet do not stay.

R.11: She is loud and does whatever she wants. \q She never stays at home.

decisions.choice: loud and defiant
decisions.reason: The first word (homiyyah) is used of Folly herself in 9:13; the second (sorer) of a stubborn, rebellious son (Deuteronomy 21:18).

decisions.choice: verses 11–12: an aside about her habits
decisions.reason: The father pauses the story to describe how she lives, then picks it up again in verse 13.

records.source: פַּ֤עַם׀בַּח֗וּץ פַּ֥עַם בָּרְחֹב֑וֹת וְאֵ֖צֶל כָּל־פִּנָּ֣ה תֶאֱרֹֽב׃
records.gloss: A time in the street, a time in the squares, and beside every corner she lies in wait.
pieces: One moment she is out in the street, \q the next in the squares, \q waiting in ambush at every corner.

L.12: A time in the street, a time in the squares, \q and beside every corner she lies in wait.

R.12: Sometimes she is in the street and sometimes in the town square. \q She waits at every corner to catch someone.

decisions.choice: street ... squares ... lies in wait
decisions.reason: She goes where Wisdom calls (1:20–21), but she lies in wait like the gang of 1:11.

records.source: וְהֶחֱזִ֣יקָהבּ֭וֹוְנָ֣שְׁקָה־לּ֑וֹ הֵעֵ֥זָה פָ֝נֶ֗יהָ וַתֹּ֣אמַר לֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And she takes hold on him and kisses him; she makes strong her face and says to him,
pieces: She grabs him and kisses him, \q and with a brazen face she tells him,

L.13: And she seizes him and kisses him; \q she makes her face bold and says to him,

R.13: She grabbed him and kissed him. \q Without any shame, she said to him,

decisions.choice: makes her face strong: shows no shame
decisions.reason: A "strong" face is a hard, unblushing one (21:29).

records.source: זִבְחֵ֣י שְׁלָמִ֣ים עָלָ֑י הַ֝יּ֗וֹם שִׁלַּ֥מְתִּי נְדָרָֽי׃
records.gloss: Sacrifices of peace offerings [are] on me; today I have paid my vows.
pieces: "I had peace offerings to make, \q and today I have kept my vows.

L.14: "Sacrifices of peace offerings [are] on me; \q today I have paid my vows.

R.14: "I went to the temple today and gave my offerings to keep my promises to God. \q I have meat from the sacrifice at home.

decisions.choice: peace offerings ... vows: she has meat at home
decisions.reason: A peace offering paid for a vow was shared: part was burned, and the worshiper ate the rest the same day or the next (Leviticus 7:15–16). She has a feast waiting and a show of religion to cover her.

decisions.choice: I have meat from the sacrifice at home
alternatives: Sacrifices of peace offerings are on me
decisions.reason: Readable says what her words imply (m1), which a young reader would not know.

records.source: עַל־כֵּ֭ן יָצָ֣אתִי לִקְרָאתֶ֑ךָ לְשַׁחֵ֥ר פָּ֝נֶ֗יךָ וָאֶמְצָאֶֽךָּ׃
records.gloss: Therefore I have come out to meet you, to seek your face, and I have found you.
pieces: That is why I came out looking for you; \q I was eager to see you, and here you are!

L.15: Therefore I have come out to meet you, \q to seek your face eagerly, and I have found you.

R.15: So I came out to find you. \q I wanted to see you, and now I have found you!

decisions.choice: seek eagerly: search hard
decisions.reason: The verb (shahar) used of those who seek Wisdom in 1:28 and 8:17. She claims to have sought him as Wisdom is to be sought.

records.source: מַ֭רְבַדִּים רָבַ֣דְתִּי עַרְשִׂ֑י חֲ֝טֻב֗וֹת אֵט֥וּן מִצְרָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: [With] coverings I have spread my couch, colored fabrics of linen of Egypt.
pieces: I have spread my couch with covers, \q with colored sheets of Egyptian linen.

L.16: [With] coverings I have spread my couch, \q colored fabrics of Egyptian linen.

R.16: I have made my bed with soft covers \q and beautiful sheets from Egypt.

decisions.choice: Egyptian linen: an expensive import
decisions.reason: Fine linen from Egypt was a luxury (Ezekiel 27:7). The wife of 31:22 makes her own coverings.

records.source: נַ֥פְתִּי מִשְׁכָּבִ֑י מֹ֥ר אֲ֝הָלִ֗ים וְקִנָּמֽוֹן׃
records.gloss: I have sprinkled my bed [with] myrrh, aloes and cinnamon.
pieces: I have scented my bed with myrrh, \q aloes and cinnamon.

L.17: I have sprinkled my bed [with] myrrh, \q aloes and cinnamon.

R.17: I have made my bed smell sweet with perfume.

decisions.choice: myrrh, aloes and cinnamon: costly perfumes
decisions.reason: The same spices perfume the lovers of the Song of Songs (4:14) and the king's robes (Psalm 45:9).

records.source: לְכָ֤ה נִרְוֶ֣ה דֹ֭דִים עַד־הַבֹּ֑קֶר נִ֝תְעַלְּסָ֗ה בָּאֳהָבִֽים׃
records.gloss: Come, let us drink our fill of love until the morning; let us delight ourselves with loves.
pieces: Come, let us drink deep of love until morning \q and take our pleasure in lovemaking.

L.18: Come, let us drink our fill of love until the morning; \q let us delight ourselves with lovemaking.

R.18: Come with me! We can make love all night long.

decisions.choice: love ... lovemaking: physical love
decisions.reason: The words (dodim, ohabim) are words for lovemaking (Song of Songs 1:2; 5:1).

decisions.choice: drink our fill: the water of 5:15–19
decisions.reason: The father told the son to drink from his own well and be satisfied with his wife's love (5:15, 19). She offers the same words for what is not his.

records.source: כִּ֤י אֵ֣ין הָאִ֣ישׁ בְּבֵית֑וֹ הָ֝לַ֗ךְ בְּדֶ֣רֶךְ מֵרָחֽוֹק׃
records.gloss: For the man is not in his house; he has gone on a journey far away.
pieces: The man of the house is away; \q he has gone on a long trip.

L.19: For the man [is] not in his house; \q he has gone on a journey far away.

R.19: My husband is away. \q He is traveling far from here.

decisions.choice: the man: her husband
decisions.reason: She does not say "my husband" but "the man", as if he were nothing to her.

decisions.choice: my husband
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly who he is.

records.source: צְֽרוֹר־הַ֭כֶּסֶף לָקַ֣ח בְּיָד֑וֹ לְי֥וֹם הַ֝כֵּ֗סֶא יָבֹ֥א בֵיתֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: The bag of the money he has taken in his hand; at [the] day of the full moon he will come home.
pieces: He took a bag of money with him \q and will not be home until the full moon."

L.20: The bag of money he has taken in his hand; \q at [the] day of the full moon he will come [to] his house."

R.20: He took a lot of money with him, \q and he will not be back for a long time."

decisions.choice: the full moon: about two weeks away
decisions.reason: The word (kese) is the full moon, a time of festival (Psalm 81:4). A bag of money means a long business journey. There is no danger of his coming back.

records.source: הִ֭טַּתּוּ בְּרֹ֣ב לִקְחָ֑הּ בְּחֵ֥לֶק שְׂ֝פָתֶ֗יהָ תַּדִּיחֶֽנּוּ׃
records.gloss: She turns him with [the] greatness of her persuasion; with [the] smoothness of her lips she impels him.
pieces: With all her powers of persuasion she wins him over; \q with her smooth talk she pushes him on.

L.21: She turns him aside with the greatness of her persuasion; \q with the smoothness of her lips she drives him.

R.21: Her sweet, clever words make him give in. \q Her smooth talk pulls him along.

decisions.choice: persuasion: the word for "learning"
decisions.reason: The word (leqah) is the "learning" the wise gain in 1:5 and 4:2. She has her own teaching, and he receives it.

decisions.choice: drives: pushes on, compels
decisions.reason: The verb (nadah) means to push or drive along.

records.source: ה֤וֹלֵ֥ךְ אַחֲרֶ֗יהָ פִּ֫תְאֹ֥ם כְּ֭שׁוֹר אֶל־טָ֣בַחיָב֑וֹא וּ֝כְעֶ֗כֶס אֶל־מוּסַ֥ר אֱוִֽיל׃
records.gloss: He goes after her suddenly like an ox to slaughter goes, and like an anklet to [the] discipline of a fool,
pieces: All at once he is following her, \q like an ox on its way to be slaughtered, \q like a fool in fetters on the way to punishment,

L.22: He goes after her at once, \q like an ox [that] goes to slaughter, \q and like an anklet to [the] discipline of a fool,

R.22: Right away he follows her, like an ox going to be killed. \q He is like a fool being led away in chains to be punished.

decisions.choice: like an anklet to the discipline of a fool, as the Hebrew text reads
alternatives: like a stag leaping into a noose (a common correction)
like a dog to the leash (the ancient Greek translation)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew line is hard to read: "like an anklet (or fetter) to the discipline of a fool". Many correct a few letters to read "like a stag stepping into a noose", which fits the arrow and the bird of verse 23. The ancient versions differ. The sense is clear: he is walking into a trap.

decisions.choice: an ox to slaughter: unaware of what is coming
decisions.reason: The ox follows quietly, not knowing where it is being led (Jeremiah 11:19).

records.source: עַ֤ד יְפַלַּ֪ח חֵ֡ץ כְּֽבֵד֗וֹ כְּמַהֵ֣ר צִפּ֣וֹר אֶל־פָּ֑ח וְלֹֽא־יָ֝דַ֗ע כִּֽי־בְנַפְשׁ֥וֹ הֽוּא׃פ
records.gloss: until an arrow pierces his liver, as a bird hurries to a trap, and he does not know that it [is] for his life.
pieces: until an arrow splits his liver; \q like a bird rushing into a snare, \q he has no idea it will cost him his life.

L.23: until an arrow pierces his liver, \q as a bird hurries into a trap, \q and he does not know that it [costs] his life.

R.23: He is like an animal about to be killed by an arrow, or a bird flying into a trap. \q He does not know that it will cost him his life.

decisions.choice: an arrow pierces his liver: a fatal wound
decisions.reason: The liver stands for the inner life (Lamentations 2:11). The arrow is the hunter's, completing the picture of the hunted animal (verse 22).

decisions.choice: his life: his very self
decisions.reason: The word (nephesh) as in 6:26: she hunts a man's life.

records.source: וְעַתָּ֣ה בָ֭נִים שִׁמְעוּ־לִ֑י וְ֝הַקְשִׁ֗יבוּ לְאִמְרֵי־פִֽי׃
records.gloss: And now, sons, listen to me, and pay attention to [the] sayings of my mouth.
pieces: So now, sons, listen to me; \q pay close attention to what I say.

L.24: And now, sons, listen to me, \q and pay attention to [the] sayings of my mouth.

R.24: So, sons, listen to me. \q Pay attention to what I say.

decisions.choice: sons: the plural address, as in 4:1 and 5:7
decisions.reason: The story is over, and the father draws the lesson for all his sons.

records.heading: Her house is the road to death

records.source: אַל־יֵ֣שְׂטְ אֶל־דְּרָכֶ֣יהָ לִבֶּ֑ךָ אַל־תֵּ֝תַע בִּנְתִיבוֹתֶֽיהָ׃
records.gloss: Let not turn aside to her ways your heart; do not wander in her pathways,
pieces: Do not let your heart drift toward her ways \q or stray onto her paths,

L.25: Let not your heart turn aside to her ways; \q do not wander into her paths,

R.25: Do not even think about going her way. \q Do not go anywhere near her.

decisions.choice: turn aside: veer off
decisions.reason: The verb (satah) is the one in 4:15, "turn aside from it", and is used of an unfaithful wife (Numbers 5:12).

records.source: כִּֽי־רַבִּ֣ים חֲלָלִ֣ים הִפִּ֑ילָה וַ֝עֲצֻמִ֗ים כָּל־הֲרֻגֶֽיהָ׃
records.gloss: for many slain she has made fall, and numerous [are] all her killed.
pieces: for she has brought down many victims, \q and those she has killed are without number.

L.26: for many [are the] slain she has made to fall, \q and numerous [are] all her killed.

R.26: She has destroyed many men. \q She has killed more than anyone can count.

decisions.choice: numerous: many, or mighty
decisions.reason: The word (atsumim) can mean numerous or strong. Strong men have fallen to her too.

records.source: דַּרְכֵ֣י שְׁא֣וֹל בֵּיתָ֑הּ יֹ֝רְד֗וֹת אֶל־חַדְרֵי־מָֽוֶת׃פ
records.gloss: [The] ways of Sheol [is] her house, going down to [the] chambers of death.
pieces: Her house is the highway into Sheol, \q sloping down to the rooms of death.

L.27: Her house [is the] ways to Sheol, \q going down to [the] chambers of death.

R.27: Going to her house is like taking the road to the grave. \q It leads straight down to death.

decisions.choice: the chambers of death: the inner rooms of the dead
decisions.reason: Her inner rooms (verses 16–17) are, in truth, the rooms of death. The chapter ends as 2:18 and 5:5 do.

decisions.choice: Sheol
decisions.reason: As in 1:12 and 5:5.
